utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, please. And I think this will be the last page, even though there are more names circled, but I will stop with this page and tender it and cease my direct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Number 39 is circled, Emil Matin. How do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Emil Matin was from Bogaljevci. He is the uncle of my brother's wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And number 40?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is his wife, Ruzica Matin, Emil Matin's wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And number 43.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Augustin Lovric, a man from Bogaljevci. Emil and Ruzica Matin were also from Bogaljevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Antunovic, that you went through the other pages and circled names that -- of people -- names that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised those -- I circled those that I recognised. For the others, perhaps if I saw the persons I would be able to recognise them. I don't know their names, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time we tender 65 ter 6201.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document shall be assigned Exhibit P11.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that would conclude my direct examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Biersay. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell will lead the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, can you hear me and understood me?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: My name is Christopher Gosnell. I represent Goran Hadzic, and I have a few questions for you. First of all, I'd like to thank you for coming and testifying here. It cannot be easy to describe some of the events that you've described. I'm going to ask you some questions. Some of them may be detailed, but some of these details may be important, and I hope that you will bear with me. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were -- at some point before you -- after you arrived in The Hague, were you informed by the Prosecution that the Defence wished to meet with you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And can you tell us what they said about that specifically?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. Could we ascertain from counsel the relevance of this to the credibility of Mr. Antunovic. I don't understand the relevance of this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it's systematically important to the credibility of all witnesses that we have an opportunity to meet with them, and that if we don't have that opportunity it's as a result of the witness declining that invitation. So I do think it's relevant to this witness and to other witnesses to ascertain, ensure, verify that indeed the witness said no after being properly informed of our request.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour? I -- perhaps I'm just not following, but it seems to be more a question about the way in which the OTP conducted itself and if, in fact, the information conveyed to counsel was correct or not about the witness's willingness to be interviewed. And I'm still a bit lost about why this line of questioning is relevant to determining the credibility of the witness and what he has told the Trial Chamber today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I had more or less the same question, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could put the question a little bit differently then and skip over this question and simply ask the witness if he could explain why he declined to speak with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Again, the issue of why he chose not to speak to the Defence, I fail to see how it's relevant to his credibility. And perhaps Mr. Gosnell can make a proffer about where he's going, because I am a bit -- it's not usual for me to be lost, but now I am truly lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, why did you decide not to meet with us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my arrival here was a great amount of pressure on me anyway. I was quite busy in the course of those days, and it must be the reason. I don't feel comfortable being here. It may have been down to fatigue or -- I don't know how to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to start off by asking you about your -- your first arrest after the JNA moved into Erdut, and you've testified that you were -- well, you first came across Sinisa Glodic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first came across the army, the individuals I mentioned, and then as I was entering Bogaljevci, I came across Sinisa Glodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. Indeed, that is what you said. Now, when you came across Sinisa, he told you to go to his cousin Stevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, how close to Dalj were you at this point when you were told to go to Stevo, or how close were you to Dalj when you actually met Stevo Glodic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A kilometre and a half, roughly. It's, in fact, a street that belongs to Dalj but is a bit further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So would it be fair to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I am under the impression that these were two different questions and now I'm a little bit lost as to what question the answer pertains: On the one hand, the distance on the moment he was told to go to Stevo, and on the other hand, when he was at Stevo's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Quite right, Your Honour. Let me clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you say you were 1.5 kilometres away from Dalj, was that when you met Stevo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that point, Sinisa Glodic was three or four houses away from Stevo Glodic. So it's all very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you'd say this was the outskirts of Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you have an understanding as to who they were at that time? In other words, in what capacity did you understand that they were arresting you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew that they were Serbs, but I don't know what sort of authorisation there was. Sinisa Glodic had weapons, and I don't know who in their right mind would not have obeyed what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did they tell you they were police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did they say anything about their affiliation at that time to a law enforcement organisation, if I can put it that broadly?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell me. Stevo told me only that I was to go to Dalj for questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did they say anything to you at the moment that they were taking you or while they were taking you about the reason that they were taking you to Dalj?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony then, you were taken to see Zeljko Cizmic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was at the culture hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember whether either of the Glodics went into the room with you with Zeljko Cizmic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did Zeljko Cizmic express any surprise that you were there when you were brought in?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't observe any sort of surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did he ask you, Why have you been brought to me, for example?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't. I said that he had asked me about the HDZ party, about my brother and the Croats in Erdut, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying he didn't ask you about anything other than the Croats in Erdut, the HDZ -- or HDZ, and your brother. No other topics were inquired about?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: He didn't ask you about weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I thought that that was understood. I said that they always had the same questions about the brother, the HDZ, the people who stayed in Erdut, the people who were armed. I can't remember really every single word that was spoken. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you say just now "that that was understood," can you tell us a little further about what you mean? Why do you say after you gave the three topics that you expressly mentioned, can you elaborate on why you say you thought that was understood?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because whenever they questioned me, I was always asked about whether anybody had any weapons among the Croats who stayed behind and, as I said, about my brother. It was always the same questions that were put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, in these questions, did they somehow, whether rightly or wrongly, I'm not asking you whether it was right or wrong, did they connect their questions about the HDZ party and about weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You don't remember whether if when they asked you about weapons they challenged you as to whether it was the HDZ party that was either providing or storing these weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If I understand your testimony correctly -- well, how long were you questioned by Mr. Cizmic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a relatively short period of time. I was taken to the cell quite soon after.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did he order that you be taken to that cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you hear him give that order to a policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear him. I would certainly not have gone there to the cell of my own accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And to whom did he give this order, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But it wasn't Sinisa Glodic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't Sinisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How far away was the cell that you were taken to from Mr. Cizmic's office?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office was upstairs, so down the steps and some 10 metres into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the cell where you were held was about 10 metres away from the entrance of the building where Cizmic was located?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And -- and this is the cell where, as you've testified, you were exposed to passers-by from the village?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not passers-by in the village. That was the building of the culture hall, and in the big yard was a market. There was no door or no ramp. Anyone from the market could reach the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on at that day that you were arrested, did anyone come and slap you or did anyone come and slap you while you were in that cell on the day that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There probably were some slaps, but I cannot really claim that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did people come along and abuse you while you were in that cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some abuses. They would spit, and that was it mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think you said there was a window in the room where you were interrogated or questioned by Mr. Cizmic. Can you tell us whether that window was facing onto the courtyard where you were located?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't facing the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cizmic come and check on you at any time while you were being held in this cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was there anyone guarding this cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a man with a rifle, an older man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you recognise him or know him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew the man by sight, and the man was -- well, he consumed a lot of alcohol. I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last name -- I will just say that I'm not sure. Milic, but as I say, I'm not 100 per cent sure. He was an older man, thin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you say that you learned that Cizmic was the chief of police. Is it correct to say that you learned this from one of the other detainees who was being held with you in that cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either from them or perhaps a bit later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was the man who was guarding you in front of your cell, was he wearing civilian clothing or any kind of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you see Sinisa Glodic while you were being held in that prison cell on the first day of your detention?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Or Stevo Glodic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you knew or were familiar with some of the other inmates that were being held with you, but you didn't know their surnames. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just said that I knew a man called Fabijancic who used to work at the IPK Vinogradi. I knew him by his last name but I do not remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you recall if there was a Slavko being held with you in that prison cell?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've testified today, I believe, or perhaps it was yesterday, that you were not beaten that night, the first night of your detention; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They did not take me out, and I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to have 2375, 65 ter 2375. And let's just start with page 1 of both documents for starters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, have you seen this document recently?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we go to page -- well, the last page of both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, on the right-hand side of your screen, do you recognise your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says there that that statement is true to the best of your knowledge and recollection; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 3 of both documents, the first full paragraph of page 3 of both documents. Now, at the very top, in fact it could be necessary to go back to the bottom line of page 2, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to read to you from page -- paragraph 6. It's not marked on the document, but it's the last line on page 2. I'm going to read it to you, Mr. Antunovic, but you do have the text in front of you. And this is what you say in your statement from 1999. You say that when you -- "When I arrived there -- when I arrived," referring to the cell, "there were already four or five people imprisoned in there, and I recognised them but did not know their names. That day I --" and this is where we need to turn the page: "That day I was sent somewhere else in the complex to clean out a room and then later sent back to the cell." And then the next paragraph is what I'm really directing your attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We seem to have a problem here, Mr. Gosnell, unless I'm mistaken, but I don't read what you read. On the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The proper ERN reference is 00822136. And there we have 135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Now I see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it's the first full paragraph on this page:

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "As it got dark, I was taken out of the room and into a nearby basement which had about a metre of water in the bottom of it." Mr. Antunovic, I want to be clear about what I'm asking you about. I'm not suggesting that this did not occur. What I'm asking you is whether perhaps you have the timing wrong now that you've read this.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I got it wrong. Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it's possible that actually you were beaten with truncheons and telephone cabling on the first night of your detention; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I cannot. There were so many things. I know what happened, but I may be wrong about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were the individuals who were present when you were beaten with cables and truncheons, were they wearing civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were they local Serbs or were they from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for those who beat me on my feet, these men were from Prigrevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Antunovic, was there one beating incident during your detention, or was there more than one beating incident, to the best of your recollection, of course?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And we are still talking about the first detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they did hit me, but I don't remember when or how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. So the witness may be escorted out of the courtroom for the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we take the second break and come back at 12.45.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm on my feet, Your Honour, because I've been informed by the Registry that there's a correction to be made, and I wondered if the Court would like me to do that while the witness is being brought in. It's with respect to a surrogate sheet for one of the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Biersay. We were told about that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- so please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So I was informed that the surrogate sheet for P3 previously had the time code 39 seconds to 3 minute and 39 seconds, and we'd requested that it be replaced with the correct time code which is 2 minute and 7 seconds to 3 minute and 24 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, we were discussing your -- your first period of detention at the Dalj police station before the break, and you testified earlier today that Mr. Cizmic cursed the individuals who had beaten you and put you in the water, and you testified that you thought "he was just doing it for the sake of form." That's at page 14, lines 24 to 25. Could you explain to us why you had that impression?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you on your feet, Ms. Biersay? No, you're not. Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I am, Your Honour. I think I will sit down until I figured out --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me. As soon as I find that reference, if I have reason to stand up, I will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I can quote. I have it in front of me just to be -- just to ensure there's no confusion. You say: "I told him what had happened, that I was forced to throw myself into the water in the basement, and he then swore at them, swearing their Chetnik mothers, but I think he was doing it just for the sake of form, because he must have known what was going on."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the question, Mr. Antunovic, is can you elaborate why you had that impression?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is my reflection, because I don't know whether he sent me to my cell to have some rest or for some other reason. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antunovic. I'd now like to move to a different topic entirely. You were a member of the youth wing of the HDZ in 1990; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly when it was that you joined?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was it before the summertime of 1990?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that I don't remember. I cannot guess either the date or the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember when you got the tattoo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1990, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you have no recollection of approximately the season when you got the tattoo, whether it was summer, fall, winter-time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you, I wouldn't like to guess or make estimates. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. Antunovic. Now, what were the activities of the HDZ or HDZ youth wing?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend the meetings and the -- perhaps it was distributing or posting leaflets or -- I don't know. As I said, I did not take part in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you take part in any HDZ activities at all?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had a membership card, but I don't remember that I ever attended a meeting or anything, no. I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know who Marin Vidic, aka Bili, is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Tomislav Mercep?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And who was he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really follow politics much. I think that he was a general in Croatia or something of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Before August 1991, do you know if he held any position?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does the name Stipan Radas ring a bell at all to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 02803. And this would be page 1 of the English, about midway down. And for the B/C/S, it starts at the bottom of page 1, and then we'll go over to page 2. Now, I understand that there are no protective measures for this witness, but if I'm mistaken on that, I'm sure I'll be corrected quickly. I'm sorry, for the individual who is being referenced here. Perhaps I -- perhaps, Your Honours, out of an abundance of caution, we ought to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, in front of you you have a document, and I won't characterise it. What I'm interested in is your knowledge of what's said in the document. And there as a sentence at that begins with "Tomislav Mercep," and I'm going to read and hopefully you can follow along in the B/C/S. It says, "Tomislav Mercep chaired the meeting." And this is referring to a meeting tend of April 1990, of the Croatian Democratic Union: "Tomislav Mercep chaired the meeting. He told us in his introductory speech that he had received instructions from the main HDZ board in Osijek to start forming a military organisation within the HDZ political party." Now, let just pause there. Does this in any way refresh your recollection as to whether a military wing of the HDZ started to be formed in the spring of 1990?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "He was to set up a technical service whose main task in the initial stage would be to arm the most trustworthy members of the HDZ, who would in fact become the first conscripts of the Croatian Army that was to formed at a later stage. Tomislav Mercep appointed Josip Gazo head of this service. The military service which was also formed at the meeting was to train the armed HDZ members in handling weapons, as well as draft a war strategy for the territory of Vukovar Municipality in case the creation of an independent Croatian state did not proceed peacefully." And it says: "Stipan Radas was appointed head of this service." Now, my question is: Did you hear about any training conducted by any part of the HDZ organisation in the use of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we can go to page 4 of this document in English and the bottom of page 7 in B/C/S. I'm sorry, the English is page 5. And this is in the first half of the page, and this is describing some of Mr. Mercep's efforts, and it says: "Money was handed over to Tomislav Mercep personally, and I do not know how the HDZ Municipal Board recorded the transfer of this money. I do know, however, that Tomislav Mercep purchased a number of Kalashnikovs using his own channels. If my memory is correct, there were about 400 pieces. The weapons were stored in the building of the Municipal Assembly and the offices of the National Defence Secretariat from where the weapons were distributed between 10 and 15 September 1991." Now, firstly, I want to ask you, in 1990, did you ever hear about Kalashnikovs being distributed by the HDZ party anywhere, in your neighbourhood or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, what was it that prompted you to get a tattoo of the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that there was something that prompted me. It just simply came to be as part of, you know, youth and all it brings, the insanity. I didn't have it done to offend anyone, and I didn't have a particular reason in doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, I -- I'm certainly not suggesting you did it to offend anyone. I'm simply trying to understand the atmosphere and mentality at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did many of your -- did any of your -- well, let me put it this way: How many of your friends, if any, also had HDZ tattoos?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there were any. I don't know. I probably felt that I was entitled to do so simply because I didn't have parents to dissuade me from doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, was it -- I'm a little bit confused. Was it an HDZ tattoo or an HDZ youth organisation tattoo? Perhaps I should put the question to the witness. Was the tattoo HDZ tattoo, or was it a tattoo HDZ youth organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There were just these three plain letters, H-D-Z, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what the tattoo looked like.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can show them to you with my hand. This was -- this was the size of the letters that I had on my upper arm here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that the witness has used his fingers to show a rectangle approximately 1 inch by 3 inches, or 2.5 centimetres by 7 centimetres, or something in that neighbourhood, if there is no objection from the Prosecution of that description.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did -- did you have any other tattoos at that time, or was that your first tattoo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who administered the tattoo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An elderly man. He was called Antun. He died several years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did he express any surprise to you that you wanted a tattoo of this nature?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, when you say that this was part of the -- and I think your words were -- your exact words were "part of the insanity of the time," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't give you a reason, because there wasn't one. I don't know how to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Antunovic, you have to understand I know very little about these events or this time, so what may be completely obvious to you may not be entirely obvious to me or to Their Honours. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I think you are referring to the insanity of the time, but the witness, if the record is correct, refers to the insanity of youth, which is not in relation to the particular time-frame. It's at 63, 9 and 10 and 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I see the record is not 100 per cent clear about the answer. Perhaps I should just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps I should clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Antunovic, you referred to insanity when I asked you about the reasons for having the tattoo put on your arm. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant was lack of concern for the future. I didn't give future much thought. I didn't have any parents to tell me what they thought about it. I just did what crossed my mine, that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sure, but you could have got an anarchy symbol. You could have got any number of other symbols. What I'm curious about is why you chose that particular symbol.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I tell you, at that time that must have seemed interesting to me. I don't think that I had a specific reason for that tattoo. I don't know what other answer I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you weren't in any way interested in politics, were you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not interested in politics today either, not in the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you went to no rallies of the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In fact, you went to no meetings of the HDZ, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You said that your best friend in around 1989, 1990, was a Serb. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdjan Oksic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And one more question about the tattoo, and I do apologise for asking all these questions --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. It isn't O-k-s-i-c. It's O-p-s-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. I'm sorry to have to go back to the tattoo, but did you pay for the tattoo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why would this elderly gentleman who administered you the tattoo do it for free?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew his son. I knew him. It was a small village. I guess he didn't object to doing it, so why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, I don't know if I've asked this already, but did you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Antun Skakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that at some point the ZNG, the National Guard Corps, arrived around Erdut; is that right? Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And they set up bases at the Vodovod resort and the TO centre in Erdut; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you recall when that happened?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the day or month.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was that before or after the combat that took place at Borovo Selo, which occurred in early May 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they had come earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you approximate how much earlier that was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. If I could, I would tell you right away. I really don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I completely understand, Mr. Antunovic. That's fine. Now, have you heard of the Croatian reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you know if they were also present either at Vodovod or anywhere in the neighbourhood of Erdut prior to the Borovo Selo incident?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I saw them. I don't know if they went about the village or not. At any rate, I don't remember seeing them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about whether it be ZNG forces or reserve police forces or any forces associated with the police driving around Erdut with guns pointed out of the back of their van as a threat to the Serb inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't either see that or hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were your Serb neighbours nervous in early 1991 about security?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what their feelings were, but it's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, you did continue to talk to your Serb neighbours in, for example, the second half of 1990 and the first half of 1991, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a small village, and I did talk to them, and I did work with quite a few Serbs at the vineyards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did any of them tell you that they were nervous about the security situation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember discussing that with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You testified about the facility at the Vodovod resort being shelled. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in late July.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you went there immediately after this shelling, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you described finding a horrifying scene of blood and burnt mattresses, if I recall correctly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The cabins or huts had burned down, as well as the items inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And your purpose in going there was to put out a fire, or did you have some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was to help with clearing the place up of the burnt mattresses and other things. I have never been a fireman myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to move to a different topic now, and it's about Marinko Lucan, and you've testified that you thought that he told the Serbian police that you had weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us what you did say or what you -- let me rephrase. What do you think Marinko Lucan told the police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably something about the HDZ, as far as I am concerned. I don't know any other reasons -- or, rather, I don't see that he would have anything else to tell them about me having done except for the HDZ party. I don't see that there would have been anything else to say about me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And he -- did he say the same thing about someone who you've called -- or who you know as Ronta, R-o-n-t-a?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I forgot that. I didn't know him, but I heard that he hailed from Sonda of Serbia -- of Sonta, that Marinko Lucan had betrayed him, had said that he had had a cafe where he used to hoist the Croatian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this Mr. Lucan, you actually witnessed him informing on Vinko Kovacevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard him say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that was during your second detention at the Dalj police station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask counsel, did he mean to say "Dalj police station" at line 22?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we have a reference to the part of the transcript where the witness talks about being detained at the Dalj police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Witness, where were you detained on that second occasion in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that culture hall. I just realised that you spoke of the police and the police station, but I did say repeatedly that I was held at the same location on that second occasion. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you learn whether or not it was true that Mr. Kovacevic had weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I think that he did say that he had one but that he had thrown it away. Now, how that happened and when, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge at all of weapons being stored in people's houses after the departure of Croatian forces from the area in early August 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, of course, that means that you didn't give any such indications to the Serbian police, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I didn't know of it simply.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've described a third period of detention where you were taken to Arkan's training centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you've described a striking event of an elderly woman being struck in the face with a truncheon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 02266, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise that document that's coming up on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see what it says, but I can't remember what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember being interviewed by Croatian judicial authorities in May 1996?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several occasions. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, do you remember meeting with an investigating judge named Ilija Bernatovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you review this document in preparation for your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember if I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to look at page 2 of the B/C/S, please, and page 3 of the English. Well, on this document, which apparently you don't -- you're not familiar with, this is what you were recorded as having said, and in the second paragraph there you'll see a description of your second detention in Dalj, and you say at the first sentence of paragraph 3: "During our stay in the prison, we had to carry out physical work in the houses of these Serbian policemen." And you've described that before the Court. And then you go on to say: "They let me out of prison after 15 days, and I went to Erdut to my uncle's place and continued doing the same job in the IPK until April 1992 when around two buses full of Croats were expelled from Erdut." Now, there's no reference at all to your detention at Arkan's training centre. Well, first of all, let me ask: Having now read that, do you have any recollection of this meeting with Mr. Bernatovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the meeting. I went there a number of times, and I gave statements, but I don't remember that specific meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were you sworn? Did you take an oath during these meetings?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not take an oath at any of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you know where your aunt was accommodated after you went to Osijek in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Osijek, she went to her brother's, to a part of Osijek which is called Senjak, to an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You say "she went to her brother's." Are you saying that she then went and lived with her brother?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a few days until accommodation was found, because this was a small studio apartment with very little space, but they had to go somewhere for a start.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how was she allocated that apartment, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: After you yourself went to Osijek, did you subsequently join the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, the regular Croatian Army, in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was that a matter of obligation? Were you conscripted, or did you join voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was of age, so I went to serve the army. Just -- it was a normal thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you see any combat action?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the regular army. These were the conscripts who were not sent to war. At least I wasn't, and other soldiers where I was were not sent to war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you say that you -- subsequent to the conflict in Croatia, you returned to -- I believe you say -- did you return to your aunt's house in 2000 -- sometime after the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you move in with your aunt?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her old house had been torn down and the Croatian state or whatever kind of assistance that was, they built a new house for my family and my brother's family. I live in the loft and my brother is on the ground floor, in the same location where the aunt's house used to stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have many others from the area also returned to their homes?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I know it may be hard to estimate or give a precise figure, but do you have an idea of how many? How many of those who left in 1991 have now returned?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say how many, but there are people who stayed in Osijek. They bought or built their own houses. I don't know how. There are also young people who tend to move to the city, and I can say that there are fewer and fewer people in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are my questions. Mr. Witness, thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Anything in redirect, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Antunovic, I have a small question to put to you: Do you think that your conditions in detention worsened when the Serbian guards discovered your tattoo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I have one question of you, Mr. Antunovic. You were asked whether over the two weeks that you were detained you had the occasion to see Arkan interacting with other people who were controlling the prison, and you said -- your answer was: "Yes. I saw him with ... Stricevic, as I said, and I think that they were in contact, and I mean Arkan and Stricevic. I say this, because whenever Arkan was not there in Dalj, in prison, Stricevic was in charge." What do you mean by whenever Arkan was not there, Stricevic was in charge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean that Stricevic also had to obey Arkan. That was my meaning, as if Arkan held a higher position than him. That's what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And was that then to say that in fact when he was there, Arkan was in charge of the prison?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO ANTUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was in charge of the prison, but what I felt was that he was somehow stronger, more powerful than Stricevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Anything from the parties come out of our questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Nothing. Thank you. Mr. Antunovic, this is the end of your testimony before this Tribunal. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague and assisting us. You may now leave the courtroom, and we wish you a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm on my feet, because I expected and the Prosecution team expected cross-examination to take a bit longer, so I'm wondering what is the Court's preference, if we take a small break so that we can switch with our colleagues, or if we adjourn for the day, or perhaps there's a third option I haven't thought of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is there anything else to be discussed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one additional pending matter which are the two documents that ought to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, let's start with that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the first document, Your Honour, that was used with the witness is 65 ter 02375. That's the prior statement of the witness signed on the 5th of May, 1999. The second document that was used with the witness was 65 ter 02803. However, we would not tender this document at this time. Our view would be that this is not yet admissible. The third document, and this is the second document, therefore, that we would tender, is 65 ter 02266. This is a record of witness interview, dated 8th of May, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So those two documents are admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2375 shall be assigned Exhibit D1. And 65 ter document 2266 shall be assigned Exhibit D2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We would say the best thing to do is call it a day, Ms. Biersay, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Court adjourned. We reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom.
